title: Subquotient bounds for Frobenius modules
statement:
If $(V,F)$ is mixed of weights at most $w$, then every
Frobenius-stable subquotient of $V$ is mixed of weights at most $w$.

proof.text: Unpack the finite stable filtration of [def-weil-frobenius-module-weights]. Fix an ambient eigenvalue alpha and a nonzero eigenvector. Induct over r in Fin (m+1) to bound the norm of alpha whenever a nonzero alpha-eigenvector lies in V_r. At r=0 the vector is zero, a contradiction. At r+1, if the vector lies in V_r use induction. Otherwise its class in V_(r+1)/(V_r comap subtype) is nonzero. The defining action-compatibility clause makes that class an eigenvector of the specified graded automorphism. Purity gives norm(iota(alpha)) = (p^a)^(w_r/2). Since p is prime, p^a >= 1, so w_r <= w gives the desired upper bound by monotonicity of real powers. V_m = top supplies the ambient bound. This works for a length-zero filtration and zero graded pieces.

proof.text: Let N be S with its canonical restricted automorphism. An eigenvector of N remains a nonzero eigenvector of M under the injective subtype map, so N has the ambient eigenvalue bound. For Q = S/U the canonical quotient map U.mkQ is surjective and intertwines N.frobeniusEnd and Q.frobeniusEnd by the defining equation of Submodule.Quotient.equiv. Apply the proved Module.End.hasEigenvalue_of_comp_eq_comp in WeilConjectures.Mathlib.LinearAlgebra.Eigenspace.Basic (the quotient-eigenvalue transfer implementing [p-linear-filtration]) to send every eigenvalue of Q to N. Hence Q has the same bound. Neither characteristic-polynomial factorization nor a stable complement is needed. Zero spaces, S=top, U=bot and U=top are included.

proof.text: Apply [lem-a1-punctual-bound-module-mixed] to the canonical quotient Frobenius module Q with exactly the given p, a, ell, algebraic closure, iota and real w. Finite dimensionality is inherited by S and its quotient, and the required invertible Frobenius is Submodule.Quotient.equiv. The eigenvalue bound from the preceding steps gives every hypothesis. Its conclusion is exactly the stated finite-filtration mixedness of Q.
